skill.name: web-design-guidelines
skill.description: Review frontend files against Vercel Web Interface Guidelines and accessibility best practices, then report issues with locations and fixes.
skill.summary: Audits UI files for design, accessibility, and UX guideline violations.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: Most command and filesystem alerts are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline examples, and related-skill links. The skill does require unpinned WebFetch access to GitHub on each review, which creates a remote content trust risk. No credential access, shell execution, or prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the GitHub raw URL to a reviewed commit or vendor a trusted copy with update notes.
Treat fetched text as reference material and keep execution rules in the local skill.
Tell users when WebFetch will run and provide an offline mode for pinned guidelines.
Use plain skill names or marketplace links instead of ../ paths to avoid traversal alerts.

content.value_statement: UI reviews can miss accessibility and interaction details. This skill checks frontend files against current Vercel Web Interface Guidelines and reports practical fixes.
actual_capabilities: Fetches Vercel Web Interface Guidelines from the configured GitHub source.
Reviews React, Vue, Svelte, HTML, CSS, SCSS, TypeScript, and JavaScript files.
Checks UI code for accessibility, UX, and interface guideline violations.
Reports issues with file and line references when evidence is available.
Suggests practical fixes for each reported violation.
limitations: It depends on an external guideline file that can change over time.
It needs user-provided files or patterns before a review can start.
It may need narrower scopes for large projects to avoid context limits.
It does not replace manual usability testing with real users.

use_cases.title: Review pull request UI changes
use_cases.description: Check changed components for guideline, accessibility, and UX issues before review.

use_cases.title: Audit design system components
use_cases.description: Find repeated interface issues across shared components and document fix priorities.

use_cases.title: Prepare accessibility review notes
use_cases.description: Identify focus, labeling, landmark, and interaction problems with clear file references.

prompt_templates.title: Review one component
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my UI code in src/components/Button.tsx. Report guideline issues with file and line references, then suggest fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a feature folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Check accessibility and UX in src/features/checkout/**/*.tsx. Prioritize issues that affect keyboard, focus, labels, and layout consistency.

prompt_templates.title: Find repeated design issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit src/components/**/*.tsx for repeated Web Interface Guidelines violations. Group findings by pattern and include representative file locations.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a release audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a final UI guideline review for src/pages/**/*.tsx and src/components/**/*.tsx. Focus on severe issues, regression risk, and concise fix guidance.

output_examples.input: Review the button component for UI guideline issues.
output: src/components/Button.tsx:15 - Icon-only button needs an accessible name.
src/components/Button.tsx:32 - Focus indicator is missing for keyboard users.

output_examples.input: Check the checkout flow for accessibility and UX problems.
output: src/features/checkout/Modal.tsx:42 - Dialog should keep focus inside while open.
src/features/checkout/Form.tsx:88 - Error message should be connected to the related field.

output_examples.input: Audit the home page before release.
output: src/pages/Home.tsx:8 - Main content should use a clear landmark.
src/pages/Home.tsx:27 - Primary action needs a visible focus state.

best_practices: Review small file groups so findings stay precise.
Fetch or pin the guideline source before each audit.
Ask for fix suggestions with each reported issue.
anti_patterns: Do not audit the whole repository in one prompt without scope.
Do not accept guideline findings without checking the cited file.
Do not use stale guideline text when current rules matter.

faq.question: Does this skill edit my UI files?
faq.answer: No. It reviews files and reports findings unless you separately ask for changes.

faq.question: Which frameworks can it review?
faq.answer: It can review React, Vue, Svelte, HTML, CSS, SCSS, TypeScript, and JavaScript files.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: The skill is designed to fetch the Vercel guideline source before review.

faq.question: Can it check accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It can flag accessibility issues covered by the fetched guidelines and visible file evidence.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: You should expect concise findings with file locations, issue descriptions, and fix suggestions.

faq.question: Is it a replacement for design review?
faq.answer: No. It helps catch guideline issues but does not replace human design review or user testing.
